def: An aircraft that flies without a pilot on board, controlled remotely or autonomously.
The complete system around a drone — the aircraft itself, the remote controller, and the communication link between them, not just the flying part.
A drone that uses several fixed-pitch propellers (commonly 4, 6, or 8) to generate lift and steer purely by varying each motor's speed.
An aircraft design that can take off and land vertically like a multirotor, then fly forward efficiently like a fixed-wing plane.
The small electronic module that sits between the flight controller and a motor, precisely regulating how fast that motor spins.
The drone's onboard computer — it reads sensor data and translates pilot commands into precise motor speed adjustments many times per second.
A satellite-based system that gives the flight controller the drone's position, enabling features like return-to-home and position hold.
A sensor combining a gyroscope and accelerometer that measures the drone's orientation and motion, used to keep it stable in flight.
The lightweight, high-current rechargeable battery type most drones use to store and supply their flight power.
The spinning blades that convert a motor's rotation into thrust, pushing air to generate lift.
The upward or forward force generated by the spinning propellers — thrust must exceed weight for a drone to climb.
Tilting the drone's nose up or down, which drives forward or backward movement.
Tilting the drone left or right, which drives sideways (lateral) movement.
Rotating the drone around its vertical axis, like turning on the spot, without necessarily moving forward or sideways.
Live flight data — altitude, speed, battery level, GPS position — transmitted from the drone back to the pilot or ground station.
Software running on the flight controller that can fly some or all of a mission automatically, without direct pilot input for every movement.
Extra equipment a drone carries beyond its own structure — most commonly a camera or sensor.
Flying using a live video feed streamed from the drone's onboard camera, as if you were sitting in the cockpit.
